what-it-is.statement: The Client Connector Dashboard (Analytics > Infrastructure > Platform Details) provides information about the organization's enrolled devices, including service status, on three pages: Platform Details (OS platform details such as device model and device state), Device Posture (devices that fail their device posture checks) and Device Events (Internet & SaaS and Private Access service status, and users turning off the services via passwords).

quotes: The Zscaler Client Connector Dashboard provides information about enrolled devices for your organization, including information about service status.
From the navigation menu, go to Analytics > Infrastructure > Platform Details.
The Dashboard option in the left-side navigation covers the following information:
This page provides OS platform details such as device model and device state.
This page provides information about devices that fail their device posture checks.
This page provides information about Internet & SaaS and Private Access service status and about users turning off the services via passwords.

platform-filters.statement: Platform Details filters by device state (all states, or a specific state such as Registered, Unregistered, Removal Pending, Removed or Quarantined) and by operating system (all or a specific one).

quotes: States: View data for devices with all device states, or a specific state (i.e., Registered, Unregistered, Removal Pending, Removed, Quarantined).
OS: View data for all operating systems or a specific operating system.

version-distribution.statement: The Version Distribution widget counts devices on supported and unsupported Client Connector versions: supported versions are enabled on the App Store's New Releases tab and listed on its Update Settings tab; unsupported versions are enabled on New Releases but earlier than the supported versions on Update Settings. Clicking the graph lists the devices, by User ID, in Enrolled Devices.

quotes: This widget displays the number of devices installed with supported and unsupported versions of Zscaler Client Connector, defined as:
Supported: Zscaler Client Connector versions enabled on the New Releases tab of the Client Connector App Store and listed on the Update Settings tab of the Client Connector App Store.

Unsupported: Zscaler Client Connector versions enabled on the New Releases tab of the Client Connector App Store but are earlier than the supported versions listed on the Update Settings tab of the Client Connector App Store.
Click the graph to view a list of all devices, by User ID, installed with either supported or unsupported versions of Zscaler Client Connector in Enrolled Devices.

model-os-state-platform.statement: The Device Model and Device OS widgets show the top 5 models and OSs and group the rest as Others; Device State shows the enrolled devices' states and the app profiles applied to them; Enrolled Devices by Platform shows their platforms. Clicking a model, OS, state or platform in its chart lists the matching devices in Enrolled Devices.

quotes: This widget displays the enrolled device models. It displays the top 5 device models and groups all other models in the Others category.
To view a list in Enrolled Devices for all devices for a specific model, click the model in the chart.
This widget displays the enrolled devices operating systems. It displays the top 5 OSs and groups all other OSs in the Others category.
To view a list in Enrolled Devices for all devices for a specific OS, click the OS in the chart.
This widget displays the states of the enrolled devices and the app profiles applied to the devices.
To view a list in Enrolled Devices for all devices for a specific state, click the state in the chart.
This widget displays the enrolled devices platforms.
To view a list in Enrolled Devices for all devices for a specific platform, click the platform in the chart.

license-usage.statement: The License Usage widget shows the organization's subscription and license information, Subscribed (the number of user subscriptions for Client Connector) against Used (the number of users enrolled); it applies only to Internet & SaaS and is not shown with Private Access only. Licenses are calculated on the unique username, so a user with Client Connector on three devices still has one license.

quotes: This widget displays your organization's subscription and license information.
This widget only applies to Internet & SaaS. You won't see this widget if you only have Private Access.
Subscribed: The number of user subscriptions for Zscaler Client Connector.
Used: The number of users that are enrolled to Zscaler Client Connector.
Licenses are calculated based on the unique username. For example, even if a user has Zscaler Client Connector installed on three devices, the user still has only one license.

device-events-availability.statement: The Device Events page is available for Windows users only and needs Digital Experience (ZDX) or Client Connector Telemetry enabled; a Time Range filter selects the time range of its data.

quotes: This page is available for Windows users only. You must also have Digital Experience (ZDX) or Zscaler Client Connector Telemetry enabled.
Use the Time Range filter to view data for the selected time range.

service-status-widget.statement: The ZIA and ZPA device service status widget counts enrolled devices with the ZDX service enabled and without it (Non-ZDX), with Internet & SaaS and with Private Access enabled, and devices that have had Internet & SaaS (Off ZIA) or Private Access (Off ZPA) turned off.

quotes: ZDX: The number of enrolled devices with the ZDX service enabled.
Non-ZDX: The number of enrolled devices without the ZDX service enabled.
ZIA: The number of enrolled devices with the Internet & SaaS service enabled.
ZPA: The number of enrolled devices with the Private Access service enabled.
Off ZIA: The number of enrolled devices that have had the Internet & SaaS service turned off
Off ZPA: The number of enrolled devices that have had the Private Access service turned off.

turn-off-widgets.statement: The service turn-off widgets count the unique users who turned the service off and the total number of times it was turned off, both even if it was turned back on; another widget shows how many times Internet & SaaS and Private Access were turned off over the past 24 hours.

quotes: Users: The number of unique users who have turned off the service, even if they have turned it back on.
Total Number: The total number of times the service has been turned off by the users, even if a user has turned it back on.
Users: The number of unique users who have turned off the service, even if they have turned it back on.
Total Number: The total number of times the service has been turned off by the users, even if a user has turned it back on.
This widget displays information about the number of times Internet & SaaS and Private Access were turned off over the course of the past 24 hours.

password-usage.statement: The Password Usage widgets count users who turned services off, users who used the Disable ZIA OTP or Disable ZPA OTP password from the enrolled device's Device Details (OTP) and users who used the app profile's Disable Password ZIA or ZPA password (Master), and the number of times ZIA and ZPA were turned off with each OTP and each master password.

evidence.after: - Password Usage - This widget displays information about the passwords used
quotes: Users: The number of individual users who have turned off the service.
OTP: The number of users who used the Disable ZIA OTP password or Disable ZPA OTP password from the Device Details for the enrolled device.
Master: The number of users who used the Disable Password ZIA password or Disable Password ZPA password from the app profile.
ZIA OTP: The number of times ZIA was turned off using the Disable ZIA OTP password.
ZPA OTP:The number of times ZPA was turned off using the Disable ZPA OTP password.
ZPA Master: The number of times ZPA was turned off using the Disable Password ZPA password.
ZIA Master: The number of times ZIA was turned off using the Disable Password ZIA password.

counting-details.title: Dashboard data retention, Time Range options and how some counts are taken
counting-details.detail: The dashboard page does not give how long Device Events data is kept or the Time Range options, how versions not enabled on the New Releases tab are counted in Version Distribution, whether Used counts removed users, or how often the widgets refresh.
